protocol.description:
Routes the device's special action key — the HUMAIN button — to a client.
The compositor owns the gesture, because the key is usually a modifier (Super) that it must also keep for its own chords, and only the compositor can tell a tap from the start of a chord. It resolves the gesture and sends the client the meaning, not the key:
- a tap sends `activate`, which asks the surface to focus its input - a hold sends `hold_start`, then `hold_end` on release, which brackets push-to-talk voice input
Clients register surfaces as receivers. When the key is used, the focused registered surface receives the event; if none is focused, the surface registered as the default receiver does. That lets a chat window take the key while it is focused and the home screen take it otherwise, without the compositor needing to identify either by app id — which a layer surface does not have.

interface.name: zcosmic_special_action_manager_v1
interface.description: Lets clients register surfaces to receive special action events.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy this manager object. Receivers created from it are unaffected.

request.name: get_special_action

description.summary: register a surface as a receiver

request.description:
Create a receiver for the given wl_surface. The surface receives events while it is focused.
If is_default is non-zero the surface also becomes the fallback receiver, used whenever no registered surface is focused. Only one default receiver exists at a time; registering a second replaces the first.

arg.name: is_default
arg.summary: 1 to also be the fallback receiver, 0 otherwise

interface.name: zcosmic_special_action_v1

description.summary: special action receiver for a surface

interface.description: Receives resolved special-key gestures for one surface.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stop receiving events for this surface.

event.name: activate
event.description: The user tapped the key. The surface should take focus of its text input so the user can start typing. No voice input is involved.

event.name: hold_start
event.description: The user is holding the key. The surface should begin capturing audio.

event.name: hold_end
event.description: The user released the key. The surface should stop capturing and process what it captured.

event.name: cancel
event.description: The gesture ended without completing — focus moved away, the session locked, or the compositor took the key back. Any capture in progress should be discarded rather than processed.
